Brian Shannon's intraday VWAP bounce: the full test report

Pass marks · Arithmetic · Controls · Limits · All trades · Reopen tests
Episode A02 · report format v2 · lab run 2026-06-11, pre-registration locked 2026-06-11 before the run
VERDICT — SELECTION ADDS INFORMATION; THE ONE-MINUTE VERSION FAILS THE COST FLOOR

The encoded bounce ranks above all 2,000 matched random-entry runs, yet averages -0.529 R per trade at 5 basis points per side. These are two different questions. Both gates had to pass; only the selection gate passed. This is a simulated result for this setup, window and stop convention.

What we granted, and what we actually tested

Granted, not measured: Brian Shannon teaches a specific touch, reclaim, new-high entry and higher-low stop. The visual check supports detecting that pattern. We grant the rule its stated rationale; the discretionary choice of stocks and tape reading are outside this test.

Tested: One intraday session-VWAP bounce, with one-minute structural stops, on 28 fixed liquid survivor stocks from 2022-04-26 through 2026-06-11. 8,636 simulated trades; fixed-fractional 1% risk; no overnight positions. Session VWAP resets every morning. This is distinct from multi-day event-anchored VWAP.

What this report does NOT claim, fixed before the run: We did not test Brian Shannon's own performance record, his whole method, or his books. No personal return series was reproduced. A mechanical translation is not his discretionary trading.

§1 · The locked pre-registration

Committed 471ae34 on 2026-06-11, before the verdict run — the wager you cannot move after seeing the cards.

The falsifiable question

Can this encoded intraday bounce clear an absolute after-cost cash hurdle AND outperform matched random entry in the same eligible stocks?

  • A yes looks like: Net annualized return at least cash + 1.0 percentage point, positive aggregate net P&L, positive net expectancy, and return above the 95th random-entry percentile.
  • A no looks like: Failure of either gate is a fail. Selection skill with sub-cash returns is recorded distinctly; it cannot be promoted into an absolute pass.
  • Ambiguous residue: Near a threshold, investigate a named plausible false-negative artifact before a terminal call. This absolute miss is not near the registered hurdle.

Our stated prior: Friction likely decisive

The registered floor recorded that the visual check "confirms detection FIDELITY, not edge" and that "the modest setup quality makes FRICTION the likely decisive factor". This was a qualitative prior, not a registered numerical probability.

Primary configuration: pre-run and run-stage decisions

Cost5 bps each side: 2 spread + 2 slippage + 1 commission

Untested scope limits — when they were identified

  1. Multi-day event anchors were identified as a reopening test after the result, not named in advance. Discretionary stock selection and tape reading remain outside this mechanical test.
  2. Gap-up handling and confluence with other indicators were identified as explicit scope limits in the later source review, after the result; they were not named in advance. Choppy-market sizing adjustments were not tested.
  3. A historical constituent universe with failures and delistings; deep bears outside this data window.
  4. Slower-chart stop reconstruction was identified after the result in the September source review, not pre-registered; it is the strongest unresolved objection.
A favorable result on a fixed survivor pool would still require broader validation. A failure applies to this encoded setup and does not establish anything about the practitioner's unmeasured returns. Both endings were disarmed on paper before the run.

§4 · The controls

Fidelity before profit: the first detector produced 13 real bounces in a 36-chart sample. Tightening the touch tolerance and excluding the unstable opening bars reduced signals from 14,799 to 8,722. The second sample contained 36 of 36 real bounces, but 31 were marginal and five were clean. We graded them ourselves, with future prices hidden. Acceptance of that disclosure was not independent re-grading. The earlier 33-marginal transcription was corrected to 31 before the result.

Signals to trades: 8,722 signals became 8,636 trades. All 86 of 86 exclusions were signals arriving while a position in that stock was already open. This bridge was counted in the September 19 rebuild.

Random-entry controls: 2,000 portfolios, seed 20260611, from pools of 1,500 structural twins per stock. Per-name trade count, long direction, eligible sessions and the bracket machinery are shared. Holding periods emerge from that machinery; their distribution was not forced to equal the system's. All controls pay the same registered fill cost. Ranking above these controls is evidence of selection value inside this comparison, not proof that the account can pay its bill.

Cost identity: over 8,636 trades, mean(0.10% of entry / risk unit) = 0.545929 R, versus the grid drop 0.545937 R. The median-trade cost is 0.405 R; the mean is higher because of the tight-stop tail. Splitting an exit into thirds does not increase total notional: the earlier explanation attributing this gap to exit granularity was wrong.

Intrabar ambiguity: 23.77% of trades contain a same-bar stop/target ambiguity. The lab's optimistic one-R-per-affected-trade bound is -0.291 R per trade, still negative. This arithmetic bound is not a full alternative fill simulation.

Sanity alarms: 0 recorded alarms; the run trades in the bear, does not depend on one trade, is not mostly closing at the bell and produces thousands of trades. These checks answer those specific questions; they do not prove an error-free simulator.

§5 · The strongest objection and what remains untested

The strongest unresolved objection is the stop timescale. Shannon describes moving from one-minute to two-minute and then five-minute charts. We kept one-minute pivot lows throughout. A wider stop changes the cost measured in R, the central mechanism here. The slower-chart rerun has NOT RUN; it is the first reopening criterion. This objection was sharpened after the original result, so it is not presented as a completed pre-registered stress test.

Two favorable-data limitations: the fixed universe contains survivors, and the stage-2 uptrend filter uses the same day's closing information, unavailable earlier in that day. The random-entry controls share the filter. This timing look-ahead limits tradability and may alter selections; a causal-filter rebuild has not been run. Neither a shared bias nor a failed net result makes the setup operationally validated.

§6 · Their own terms

Source: TraderLion, The AVWAP Trading Indicator | Secrets and Setups | Brian Shannon, CMT. The entry-rule passage is at 48:01. The taught sequence is touch, reclaim, first new high after the touch, and stop under the relevant higher low. Our numeric choices and simulator conventions are distinct from that teaching.

The following 26 choices are the rule-to-code ledger. Detector and floor choices were frozen at the June 11 ratification. Simulation conventions 18 through 26 were appended during the result-stage implementation under the registered allowance; they are not represented as earlier separately committed decisions.

§7 · The complete ledger — all 8636 rows

Every 8,636 of 8,636 recorded trades is rendered and downloadable. This archive records entries, stops, targets, exit-bar indices and event reasons. It does not contain a realized net-return column per trade; aggregate return tables above come from the run's archived metrics. The cost identity and holding-time summary can be recomputed from this CSV. Prices are in dollars; bars count from the session start; entry_min is minutes after midnight in New York; risk_unit is entry minus the average initial stop. t1/t2 name the first and second targets. Event names describe target, breakeven, stop, trailing-stop or end-of-day exits. Check our arithmetic: the ledger fields support the cost calculation; archived run summaries supply aggregate returns.

§8 · What would change our mind

  1. Slower-chart stops (NOT RUN): keep the same entries, rebuild stops from two-minute and five-minute lows, and price them at the same five basis points per side. Register the run before looking. The episode proposes average cost below 0.10 R and positive mean net R at that cost as the specific result that would make this a timescale finding. Those are future-test criteria, not claims about a completed run.
  2. Multi-day anchored VWAP (NOT RUN): test earnings, gap or IPO anchors at swing cadence with wider stops. This is a separate setup and could pass without contradicting this intraday result.
  3. Deeper bear windows (NOT RUN): add 2020 and late 2018 with suitable data. This window does not answer those regimes.
  4. Historical universe including dead and delisted stocks (NOT RUN): replace the fixed survivor pool. Our expectation is less flattering results; if it improves them, that expectation was wrong.
  5. A named data or simulator defect: supply a reproducible counterexample. The cost identity and the stated bracket bound address particular suspects, not every possible error. Positive costs below the smallest tested positive grid cell have not all been simulated; the linear breakeven estimate is an interpolation, not a broker quote.

§9 · What survives

The visual sample supports that the detector finds the taught pattern, and the matched comparison supports selection value inside this window. Those results survive alongside the absolute after-cost failure. They say nothing about an unmeasured personal record. The general check is to express execution cost and gross expectancy in the same risk units; whether it supports a different strategy requires that strategy's evidence.

§10 · Want to run a test like this yourself?

Everything we make is free — the reports, the ledgers, all of it. The only thing that costs us real money is the market data.

The equity history behind this report is a one-shot pull from Polygon.io (now Massive.com): 11,769,752 one-minute rows across the fixed 28-stock universe, plus Polygon daily closing prices for the same stocks, which feed the stage-2 uptrend filter. Both series are split-adjusted. The cash comparison uses the 13-week Treasury-bill rate (^IRX), sourced from Yahoo Finance via yfinance. No options data was used. The market-data affiliate below is EODHD, a different vendor; it did not supply this test's prices. The source provider has no say in the verdict.
